Welcome to the third league!

New: stamina. Every tensed muscle costs stamina, every hit taken drains it, and a tired fighter is weaker.

 The Goal

Two fighters face each other in a ring seen from the side. Each bot drives one of them: a physical body of 19 points moved by 15 joint motors. Land strikes, keep the balance and stay in the ring: the winner brings the opponent to 0 HP, or has more HP after 250 turns.

Source code of the game (referee, physics engine, viewer): github.com/mehdiAyari/byte-club

 Rules

The ring

  • The ring is shown in a side view, with all coordinates expressed in millimetres. The origin is at the top left of the scene: x grows to the right, y grows downward, and the floor is at y = 3000.
  • The ring is 6 m wide: from x = 2000 to x = 8000. Its centre is at x = 5000.
  • Each player sees the match from the left: in its input, its own fighter stands on the left and faces right. The fighter on the right reads the scene mirrored (x becomes 10000 − x, vx becomes −vx). Every command has the same effects relative to each player's perspective.
  • Both fighters start in STANCE, at rest, startDistance apart (1600 to 2400, an even number, drawn at random), on either side of the centre. A fighter faces the same way for the whole match.
  • Each fighter starts with 100 HP.

The fighter

A fighter consists of 19 points connected by 20 rigid bones, with a total mass of 65.4 kg. Both fighters are right-handed boxers standing face-to-face. LEAD refers to the side in front, while REAR refers to the other side.

8REAR_SHOULDER2606 REAR_GIRDLE
9REAR_ELBOW1.5507 REAR_SHOULDER

  • Each row of the table is one point, with its own mass and radius. Each joint turns exactly one bone, and is listed on the row of the point at the far end of that bone: for example, the joint LEAD_SHOULDER turns the upper arm around the point LEAD_SHOULDER, so it is on the row of the point LEAD_ELBOW.
  • Bones, in mm:
    • the spine: NECK–HEAD 200, CHEST–NECK 180, WAIST–CHEST 180, PELVIS–WAIST 140;
    • each arm: NECK–SHOULDER 130, SHOULDER–ELBOW 300, ELBOW–HAND 280;
    • each leg: PELVIS–KNEE 450, KNEE–ANKLE 450;
    • each foot, a rigid triangle of 3 bones (ANKLE–HEEL, ANKLE–TOES, HEEL–TOES): the heel is 50 behind and 60 below the ankle, the toes are 170 in front of and 60 below the ankle.
  • A point is considered to touch the floor when the distance between its centre and the floor is less than its radius. Standing flat, the centres of the heels and toes are 30 mm above the floor (y = 2970).
  • Against the other fighter, a body is made of round shapes (radius in mm):
    • the head: a circle of radius 110 around HEAD;
    • the torso: three capsules NECK–CHEST, CHEST–WAIST and WAIST–PELVIS, of radius 130, 120 and 130;
    • the upper arms: capsules SHOULDER–ELBOW of radius 50; the forearms: capsules ELBOW–HAND of radius 45;
    • the gloves: circles of radius 65 around the hands;
    • the thighs: capsules PELVIS–KNEE of radius 80; the shins: capsules KNEE–ANKLE of radius 50;
    • the feet: capsules HEEL–TOES of radius 30;
    • the knees: circles of radius 75 around the knees, which only strike.
  • A fighter never collides with itself.

Joints and motors

15 joints, each driven by a motor, in this order:

#Joint0°Positive anglesRange of rotation (°)Max torque (N·m)Max speed (rad/s)
0NECKhead in line with the upper backhead forward, chin tucked-30 to 454010
1UPPER_BACKstraightbent forward-20 to 3512010
2LOWER_BACKstraightbent forward-25 to 4015010
3, 6LEAD_GIRDLE, REAR_GIRDLEshoulder on the torso line, under the neckshoulder forward-60 to 6012015
4, 7LEAD_SHOULDER, REAR_SHOULDERarm hanging along the torsoarm raised to the front-60 to 1808040
5, 8LEAD_ELBOW, REAR_ELBOWarm straightelbow bent0 to 1506060
9, 12LEAD_HIP, REAR_HIPthigh in line with the torsothigh raised to the front-45 to 13022025
10, 13LEAD_KNEE, REAR_KNEEleg straightknee bent0 to 15022050
11, 14LEAD_ANKLE, REAR_ANKLEsole at a right angle to the shintoes pointed down-40 to 5015020
  • A row with two joints gives the values of each of the two. Max speeds are in rad/s, the unit used by the physics engine: 1 rad/s is about 57.3°/s, so 10 rad/s is about 573°/s.
  • Girdles, shoulders and hips are measured from the torso line (neck to pelvis), every other joint from the bone before it, in each fighter's own frame: the same command makes the same move on both sides.
  • Each motor pulls its joint toward its target angle with a torque capped at strength (0 to 100 %) × max torque, the full cap 10° away from the target (5° for the ankles). Like a muscle, it gets weaker as it moves faster, down to 0 at the max speed. Strength 0 leaves a joint limp; a range is a hard stop; targets and strengths stay until they are changed.

A turn

  1. Both bots send a command at the same time.
  2. Each turn represents 0.1 seconds of fighting, simulated in 40 steps of 2.5 milliseconds. At every step the bodies move and push against each other, and the strikes that land are detected.
  3. At the end of the turn, everything is settled: the HP taken by the strikes, the stamina, the falls and ring-outs, and the end of the match.

A match lasts at most 250 turns: 25 seconds of fighting.

Commands

Each turn, a bot writes one line with one of these commands:

  • A move from the table below, one frame per turn. A held pose (STANCE, GUARD, RELAX, DUCK) lasts as long as it is sent. A timed move lasts the number of turns given: sending the name of the move again, or WAIT, lets it go on; any other command interrupts it at once. At its end, the fighter is back in STANCE, and sending the name of the move again starts it over.
  • WAIT: a running move goes on and a held pose is held. After JOINTS, the motors keep their targets and strengths.
  • JOINTS t1 s1 t2 s2 ... t15 s15 sets the 15 motors directly, in the joint order: a target in degrees and a strength in % for each joint.
    • Each value is a number (an optional minus sign, up to 6 digits, optionally a point and up to 6 decimals), or * to keep the current value. A target is rounded to 0.01°, a strength to a whole number.
    • ROUND (in capitals) after the 30 values swings the lead leg around the opponent's body for this turn, as HIGH_KICK does (see Strikes).
    • JOINTS stops the running move. The legs then only follow their targets: the engine no longer places the feet nor keeps the balance.
    • Example: JOINTS, 14 *, 10 100, 14 * drops the rear arm (joint 7 to 10° at 100 %) and keeps every other motor as it is.

Any text after the command is a message, shown above the fighter (40 characters at most). After JOINTS, the message must not start with a number or *.

The line may start with LOOK skin hair to choose the fighter's look on the first turn (example: LOOK 3 5 STEP_FORWARD; alone, it is a WAIT).

  • skin: 0 (very light) to 7 (very dark).
  • hair: 0 black, 1 dark brown, 2 brown, 3 light brown, 4 dark blond, 5 blond, 6 auburn, 7 ginger, 8 grey, 9 bald.

Shorts and gloves are in the player's colour.

MoveTurnsWhat it does
STANCEheldboxing stance: lead foot forward, rear foot 42 cm behind it, knees slightly bent, lead glove at eye level, rear glove at the chin
GUARDheldhigh guard: both gloves in front of the face, arms held firmer, chin tucked
RELAXheldarms hanging at 10 % strength: cheaper in stamina, but the head is open
DUCKheldback bent forward, chin down, gloves up, a quarter of the way down per turn: fully ducked after 4 turns, the head about 35 cm lower
JAB3lead straight in 1 turn, the pelvis 11 cm forward over the feet; then 2 turns back to the stance
CROSS3rear straight in 2 turns, the pelvis 9 cm forward; then 1 turn back
OVERHAND4the rear arm loads high (2 turns), then comes down over the opponent's gloves (1 turn); then 1 turn back
KICK6lead-leg kick: weight onto the rear foot, knee up, kick, knee back, foot down, on one leg meanwhile
HIGH_KICK12lead-leg round kick to the head: the leg swings up and around the opponent's body, then comes back down
STEP_FORWARD7the lead foot goes about 25 cm forward, then the rear foot follows it
STEP_BACK7the rear foot goes first, then the lead foot follows it
JUMP7crouch, push off with both legs, knees tucked in the air, landing: the feet leave the floor by about 30 cm

Wrong lines. A line that is not a command (empty, or an unknown name: names are in capitals) loses the match. A command that is recognized but cannot be played as written is not played: the console says why, and WAIT is played instead (for example JOINTS with a value missing, one too many, or a value that is not a number). A value out of its range is played as the closest valid value, and the console says so. A LOOK that cannot be used (a later turn, other values) is ignored, with a message, and the rest of the line is played.

Legs and balance

A fighter keeps its balance while its weight point stays over its feet: the x of its centre of mass plus the horizontal speed of the centre of mass × √(height of the centre of mass above the floor ÷ 9.81), in m and m/s.

  • For the held poses, the punches and the steps, the engine runs the legs at 100 % strength: it places the pelvis above the feet, the ankles lean against where the weight goes, and the feet are put back 42 cm apart when they drift more than 6 cm from that spacing (15 cm while ducked).
  • Balance step: when the weight point goes more than 2 cm past the feet, a foot steps and lands under the weight point. The game summary reports these steps.
  • Walking (STEP_FORWARD, STEP_BACK): a fighter whose weight is not placed for the step (after a push, a strike, or at speed) first keeps its balance: its legs hold its place for a turn, as in a held pose, then its step starts again. Otherwise the feet only go the way of the step: a step back while the weight goes forward (or the reverse) can make the fighter fall.
  • KICK, HIGH_KICK and JUMP leave the legs to their own targets: no help with the balance. So does JOINTS.
  • rise (0 to 4) counts how many quarters deep the fighter is ducked: DUCK adds one, the other poses and the punches take one away, and a kick, a step or JUMP (or JOINTS) sets it back to 0.

The exact conditions of these steps are in the Expert Rules. The exact numbers of the legs are in the source code (Game.java).

Strikes

  • Gloves, knees and feet strike. Gloves and knees score on the head and the torso; feet also score on the thighs, shins and feet. Zone: head 2, torso 1, legs 0.5.
  • A strike scores when the striking part touches the opponent while the two close in at 2 m/s or more, and the striking part itself moves toward the target at 1 m/s or more. Damage = zone × (closing speed − 2), with the closing speed in m/s capped at 12, rounded to the nearest whole number (halves up). Example: a glove landing on the head at 7 m/s takes 10 HP.
  • A strike on an upper arm or a forearm is blocked: no damage. Touching a glove deals nothing either.
  • One hit per contact: a striking part scores again only after it has been away from the opponent for 10 physics steps (25 ms). A foot scores only where it touches at least 30 cm above the floor. Nothing scores once a fighter is down.
  • Depth: each fighter's lead side faces the other's rear side. A lead limb passes beside the opponent's lead limbs and meets its rear limbs, head and torso; a rear limb meets the opponent's lead limbs, head and torso. So a JAB can only be blocked by the rear arm, a CROSS by the lead arm. The legs pass beside each other, except that a lead foot meets the rear thigh.
  • Round kick: during HIGH_KICK (or a turn of JOINTS ... ROUND) the lead leg goes around the opponent's body: it meets only the head, and the rear forearm and glove while that glove is held high.
  • Every contact also pushes: the two bodies never overlap, and a blocked strike can still knock a fighter off balance.

The strikes against a fighter holding a pose, 0.8 to 0.9 m away (distance between the two PELVIS points), measured with the referee:

Strikeon STANCEon GUARDon DUCK
JAB3 HP (head)00
CROSS4 to 7 HP (head)1 to 2 HP0
OVERHAND7 HP (head)3 to 4 HP0
KICK3 to 4 HP (thigh)3 to 4 HP3 HP
HIGH_KICK5 to 6 HP (head) from 0.85 m; less closer7 to 12 HP (head): it goes around the guard0

These values are those of the ready-made strikes. A strike built with JOINTS can land faster, up to the cap of the formula (20 HP on the head), and no held pose stops every strike.

A ducked head is lower and ahead of its feet: the punches go over it from 0.8 to 0.9 m, and reach it from farther away. JAB: 4 to 8 HP from 1.10 to 1.24 m. CROSS: 4 to 7 HP from 1.06 to 1.24 m. OVERHAND: 4 to 9 HP from 1.20 to 1.36 m.

Falls and ring-outs

  • Only the feet (ankles, heels and toes) may touch the floor. When any other point touches it, the fighter is down. When any point touches the floor outside the ring (x below 2000 or above 8000), the fighter is out.
  • A split too deep is a fall too: at the end of a turn, a fighter whose ankles are more than 800 apart in x while its pelvis is less than 45 cm above the floor (y above 2550) is down.
  • A down or an out costs 20 HP. After a push, it costs 10 HP: a push is when the fighters touched during that turn or the 20 turns before, and no strike took HP in that time.
  • After a turn with a down or an out, both fighters go back to their starting places, in STANCE and at rest. HP and stamina stay as they are.

Stamina

  • Stamina is counted in thousandths of a percent: 100000 is 100 %, the start and the most.
  • Each turn, before its physics, a fighter gets back 4.84 % and pays for the tension of its motors: each joint costs its strength (in %) × 0.004 % for the neck, the backs and the joints of the legs, 0.006 % for the girdles, 0.008 % for the shoulders and the elbows. A move costs the strengths of its own frame.
  • A strike that takes n HP also takes n % of stamina, at the end of the turn.
  • A tired fighter is weaker: the torque cap of every motor is multiplied by 0.4 + 0.6 × stamina ÷ 100 %.

Stamina won (+) or spent (−) over a whole move, turn regain included, when no hit lands and the move starts at 98 % or less:

MoveStaminaMoveStamina
STANCE+0.24 % per turnOVERHAND (4 turns)−6.12 %
GUARD−1.04 % per turnKICK (6 turns)−0.82 %
RELAX+1.20 % per turnHIGH_KICK (12 turns)−0.91 %
DUCK−1.04 % per turnSTEP_FORWARD (7 turns)−0.84 %
JAB (3 turns)−1.64 %STEP_BACK (7 turns)−0.50 %
CROSS (3 turns)−4.00 %JUMP (7 turns)+1.13 %

Stamina never goes over 100 %: what a turn would add above it is lost. A JUMP started at 100 % ends at 100 %, and a HIGH_KICK started at 100 % costs 1.51 %.

Victory Conditions
  • Bring the opponent to 0 HP or less (a knockout).
  • Have more HP than the opponent after 250 turns.
  • Have more HP than the opponent when the fighters have not touched for 150 turns: the match stops there.
The same HP at the end, or both fighters at 0 HP in the same turn, is a draw.
Loss Conditions
  • Reaching 0 HP, or having fewer HP than the opponent when the match ends.
  • Writing a line that is not a command, or not answering in time: the match is lost at once (a draw if both players do it in the same turn).

 Expert Rules

  • The input is the whole state of the match. The engine is on GitHub (classes Game, Physics, Moves and Command). A copy rebuilt with Game.fromInput holds the player's fighter as fighter 0, on the left, as the input shows it: given both commands (apply(0, ...) for the player, apply(1, ...) for the opponent), it computes exactly the next input, inputLines(0). Only the opponent's command is unknown.
  • Nothing is random during a match. Only the starting distance is drawn; in the IDE, the game parameter distance sets it.
  • A physics step only uses additions, subtractions, multiplications, divisions and square roots on 64-bit floating-point numbers: it gives the same numbers in every language.
  • A step of 2.5 ms: gravity and the motors change the speeds, the points move, the strikes are detected (their HP are taken at the end of the turn), then the bones, the joint ranges, the contacts and the floor are enforced. The contacts between the fighters are solved in both orders and averaged: a match and its mirror image play the same. The exact order and the motor law are in Physics.java.
  • At the end of a turn, positions are rounded to the millimetre and speeds to the millimetre per second (halves to the even number): the next turn starts from exactly what the input says. The angles of the input are worked out from the points and rounded, the targets are exact; a joint's speed can be worked out from the speeds of the points (Physics.angSpeed).
  • Legs and balance, the exact conditions of the steps.
    • Both feet on the floor: when the weight point goes more than 2 cm past the feet (ahead of the front toes or behind the rear heel) while both feet are on the floor, the foot the weight is leaving steps past the other foot and lands under the weight point.
    • With one foot in the air, as soon as the weight point goes more than 2 cm past the foot on the floor, the foot in the air comes down under it (or at its place of the stance when that is farther); a foot already more than 6 cm past the weight point goes no farther (it comes down where it is, or, with the feet more than 70 cm apart, closer to the body when it has gone past its landing place), and a foot that is lifting off does not count as the foot on the floor.
    • With the feet more than 80 cm apart, the pelvis no longer sinks to reach both feet: it stays above the foot it goes to, and the other foot follows sooner.
    • From 70 cm apart, during a step, the other foot already follows as soon as the weight point is past the middle of the feet and the pelvis goes toward the first foot slower than 0.15 m/s.
    • A foot that hangs in the air while the pelvis and that foot both move slower than 0.05 m/s is put down where it is.
    • A fighter that walks (STEP_FORWARD, STEP_BACK) first keeps its balance: at the start of a turn, its legs hold its place for that turn as they do in a held pose, balance steps included, and its step starts again from its first turn after, in each of these cases:
      • its centre of mass goes the way of the step faster than 1.3 m/s (0.7 m/s in STEP_BACK);
      • its centre of mass goes the other way faster than 0.3 m/s while its weight point is past the foot that the step leaves on the floor (behind the heel of the rear leg's foot in STEP_FORWARD, ahead of the toes of the lead leg's foot in STEP_BACK);
      • on the first turn of a step, its weight point is less than 13 cm in front of the rear heel (or behind it), or, in STEP_BACK, less than 13 cm behind the front toes (or ahead of them);
      • on a later turn of a step, its weight point is more than 10 cm past the feet on the side opposite to the step (behind the rear heel in STEP_FORWARD, ahead of the front toes in STEP_BACK);
      • the step follows GUARD, RELAX, DUCK, a punch or a step that held its place, and either the legs of a held pose take a balance step on this turn, or a foot is in the air (its heel and its toes both higher than 45 mm; they are at 30 mm on the floor), or, in STEP_FORWARD, the torso line (from the pelvis to the neck) leans more than 30° forward.
    • Feet that are only out of place do not hold a walker: its step puts them back.
    • When the weight point goes more than 2 cm past the foot that steps first (ahead of its toes in STEP_FORWARD, behind its heel in STEP_BACK), that foot steps again at once, without waiting for the next move.
    • In the first 3.5 turns of a step, while both feet are on the floor and the foot that steps first is behind the other foot the way the step goes (crossed feet: the lead leg's foot behind the rear leg's foot in STEP_FORWARD, the rear leg's foot ahead of the lead leg's foot in STEP_BACK), that foot stays on the floor until the weight point is on the other foot, at least 2 cm ahead of its heel in STEP_FORWARD or 2 cm behind its toes in STEP_BACK; until then both legs push the weight point there.

 Game Input

Initialization input
First line: one integer startDistance: the horizontal distance between the PELVIS points of the two fighters at the start, in mm.
Input for one game turn
4 lines. The player's own fighter always comes first, and is seen on the left (see The ring): x grows to the right and y downward, in mm and mm/s.
First 2 lines: 6 space-separated values hp stamina moveName frame rise roundKick (moveName is a string, the others are integers), for the player's fighter, then for the opponent: HP; stamina in thousandths of a percent (0 to 100000); the move the fighter is in, and how many of its turns have been played (0 for a held pose); after a JOINTS command, the move is JOINTS and the frame 0; how deep the fighter is ducked (0 to 4 quarters); 1 when its lead leg went around the other body last turn (round kick), else 0.
Next line: 304 space-separated values: 8 values x y vx vy apart angle target strength for each of the 38 points (angle and target are decimal numbers, the others are integers): the player's 19 points, then the opponent's, in the order of the points table.
  • x y vx vy: position and speed of the point. For example, the distance between the two pelvises is the x of the opponent's PELVIS (point 23 of the line) minus the x of the player's (point 4).
  • apart: the physics steps since the striking part at this point last touched the other fighter (0 to 10; it can score again at 10). The gloves are at the hands, the feet at the toes, the knees at the knees; 10 for the points that do not strike.
  • angle target strength: the motor of the joint that moves this point (see the points table), as it is now, legs run by the engine included: angle and target in degrees (2 decimals), strength in %. 0.00 0.00 0 for WAIST, PELVIS and the heels, which no joint moves. Read in order without these four points, the points give the joints in the joint order.
Last line: 2 space-separated integers sinceContact sinceHit: turns since the fighters last touched, and since a strike last took HP (0: during the last turn). Both are 21 at the start and after a fall; sinceContact counts up to 150, sinceHit up to 21.
Output for one game turn
One line: a command (see Commands), optionally followed by a message.
Constraints
1600 ≤ startDistance ≤ 2400
Response time for the first turn ≤ 1000 ms
Response time per turn ≤ 50 ms
At most 250 turns
